accessibility.text: Could technology allow me to indefinitely delay death?
For biological systems, death seems inevitable. Biological systems age and decay over time, and there is (so far as we know) no way to prevent this from happening.
Could technology allow me to indefinitely delay death?

Recent technological developments, though, have led many to pose the question of whether we might be able to indefinitely delay death, not by stopping or slowing the biological aging process, but by escaping our biological nature entirely.

Could technology allow me to indefinitely delay death?

We might attempt to do this by becoming, not biological systems, but synthetic artificially intelligent systems. This possibility has been taken increasingly seriously in recent decades. A central idea of the transhumanist movement has been that advances in computing power will, as early as a few decades from now, make ‘whole brain emulation’ possible. This would involve the creation of a digital replica of a human brain, which would preserve its memories, personality, and consciousness.
